I find it mind boggling that people expect someone with no technical expertise to lead a team of engineers. An engineer can be a manager it's much easier to go from a technical background to a business background than the other way.

I find it mind boggling that people expect someone with no technical expertise to lead a team of engineers.

Happens all the time, for better or worse. Often people who become CEO are businesspeople and not engineers themselves. Even if they were engineers at one point, their tech knowledge is quite stale. Technical issues are details for the technical people to figure out, not the other way around.

Even if an engineer becomes manager, the shareholders are probably people with a financial background - not even a 'business' (=management) background. As far as they are concerned, their shares are viewed abstractly as a vehicle for financial return, and the details - whether managerial, organizational, or technical - are unimportant. Their role is to define the return-on-equity they expect, and it's up to the Ellen Pao's and their Admins to figure out how to do that.

I interned at a energy grid software company. We employed a lot of electrical engineers and computer scientists. The company was founded/run by a man with a Phd in Electrical Engineering. I was in the finance department so we were managed by the CEO's wife who treated us like the unimportant admin staff we were. So it is possible for someone from a technical background to still lead a large company. As for shareholders just wanting returns I can see how that happens.

And this is why businesses fail all the time.

If the CEO has no technical background that business is guaranteed to be a sub-par shithole. Sometimes even having a tech background is not enough and you need even more of it.

The CEO is there for the corporate vision. Vision never comes from the business side, it always comes from the tech side. CEO with no technical background means a company without vision. It is guaranteed to go stale, be outcompeted and go to the dogs.

Take HP for example. In the 60's and 70's they had engineers and scientists at the top and they were a technology powerhouse. Their test and measurement equipment was what made the Apollo program possible. What are they today? A consumer goods company, totally irrelevant.

Compare and contrast to Intel which has always been headed by a tech at the top.

Downloaded it this morning on Android. It's ok. Initial impressions:

Pros:

  • All official SW content in one place - Youtube videos, trailers, SW.com posts, and official social media Facebook, Twitter, Instagram, etc.

  • The animated reaction GIF library is pretty cool

  • Soundboards don't have too much content, but the audio quality is good. They isolated the vocal/SFX tracks so you don't get any background noise from the movies.

  • Kittster avatar is available. /s

Cons:

  • I have a Moto G, and my poor 1GB of RAM struggles with this app. My desktop refreshes every time I exit. Seems like a resource hog.

  • I like the film countdown and weather features, but it would be nice if they had widgets available. Having to open the app to view these makes them almost pointless.

  • The Force trainer feature seems buggy. I couldn't seem to get it working.

Summary: Seems like a lot of potential here, though those widgets seem like they would be a no-brainer. Nice to have all official SW content in one place. You may have issues if you have an older phone, or 1GB of RAM.
